title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Ulla’s student who always spoke in Ulla’s name, as in Berakhot 8a, Shabbat 17b, 79a and 110a (in Gittin 22a, “Rabbi Chiyya bar Assi said in Ulla’s name,” and Hyman proposes bar Ami), Bava Batra 163a, Sanhedrin 26a [according to Dikdukei Soferim] and Avodah Zarah 37a. In Avodah Zarah 23b: “Rav Nachman, Ulla and Avimi bar Pappi were sitting, and Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami was sitting with them.” In Chagigah 25b, “Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba in Ulla’s name: A beit peras that was trodden is pure” — Tosafot on Bekhorot 29b read Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami. In Arakhin 28b he spoke in the name of Cholfana (or Ulpana).

Well known is the saying cited in his name in several places: “His betrothed wife — he is not an onen and does not become impure for her,” etc. The source is Ketubot 53a, where he said to Rav Nachman, Ulla and Avimi bar Pappi: “We have learned: His betrothed wife,” etc. From this it is cited in Bava Metzia 18a in the phrase “as it was taught,” and in Yevamot 43b “but it was taught.” In Sanhedrin 28b Hyman regards as an error the reading “as Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami said in Ulla’s name”; he proposes “as it was recited in a baraita.” In Yevamot 29b the words “bar Ami” are missing; in Ketubot 89b, “as Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin taught,” Hyman proposes bar Ami; and in Sanhedrin 43b, “Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav Chisda said,” Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami.

notes.text: Chiyya is the student reporting Ulla, not Ulla reporting Chiyya. The supplied Avodah Zarah23b locator remains alongside the earlier parallel-notice53b comparison, without a fresh matching-locus claim here. All Assi/Ami/Abba/Avin/Ashi and reciter/transmission corrections remain Hyman’s proposals.

Ketubot 53a directly names Nachman, Ulla, Avimi bar Rav Pappi and Chiyya bar Ami in the sitting scene and the betrothed-wife baraita. Bounded normalized-name checks of the consulted Avodah Zarah 23b and 53b did not match that scene; these checks are not claims of absence. Hyman’s supplied locator, name corrections and reciter-versus-transmitter emendations are retained with this qualification.
